reviews.body:
There are 2 main issues here:
1. We're relying on "OracleConnection" being the type (eg. if it's wrapped, that won't work).
2. The abstraction isn't correct due to that - it's very much the goal that the the core code does _not_ know about each provider. That violates the provider model.

The Oracle bits should be an adapter that plugs into the model. Consider a wider example: if we had to know about every database provider in the core path (e.g. `Get<T>`), we'd have to add every provider, every version (with differences), and have no extensibility. Instead, the provider should be flexible enough to support the various providers and the provider needs plugin there.

In this case, we'd need to extend the provider interface in `.Contrib` and that's breaking, so at a minimum it'll have to wait for v3...but we're honestly not sure what we want to do there. The current model has several issues and we need to look at Contrib separately from the main upgrades in a few areas like this that need more cross-provider love. In short, it's a set of problems specific to generating SQL, which core Dapper largely doesn't have.

I'm trying not to make assumptions here but may be forgetting some critical context so...does the above make sense? Happy to add context if not!

This PR also changes a lot of other things (breaking the build). In this case, it appears:
- You're using an older version of visual Studio (indicated by the service GUID added to the tests .csproj).
- The entire `Dapper.Tests.csproj` has a whitespace delta (always watch for these on commit!).
- The connection strings have been changed (your IPs are in there).
- The Hana tests are loaded unconditionally, but it's only built for .NET 4.5 - we need a build for each to test this (ideally through NuGet).

If we can clean the above us, we can get a better idea of where we're at, but the last one is a pretty big item.

What are the chances Hana can provide a NuGet package? To see any widespread usage (and be worth maintaining it), it needs a package. To test it, we have to setup a server and none of our test facilities have this either. But let's see if we can get anywhere on the package front first :)
